subject: Request: payment rhythm exemption for Greenline Health (quarterly invoices, extended remit)

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Subject: Proposal for payment-rhythm exemption (Greenline Health)

Hi Oliver —

Thanks again for a productive call this morning. Per our conversation, Greenline is asking for two non-standard billing items for the pilot year: 1) quarterly invoices (instead of monthly) and 2) Net-90 payment terms. I wanted to document the ask and escalate for approval so we can move the SOW to signature.

Options I recommend to mitigate Redwood risk:
- 25% upfront payment on signature (applied to first invoice)
- Rolling security deposit (equivalent to one quarterly invoice) held for first 6 months
- Add 1.5%/month late-fee clause after Net-60 to encourage on-time payment

If execs approve, legal will add the conditional language to the SOW and our finance team will generate the invoice schedule. Attached: Greenline_SOW_v1.2.pdf and the credit form Greenline_credit_form_filled.pdf.

Oliver — can you confirm Greenline cannot move to Net-60 or provide partial prepay? That will help the approval ask.

Next steps I propose:
1) I escalate to Sales Ops/Finance for formal approval (this thread)
2) If approved, legal to add terms and we arrange the initial payment schedule

Thanks,
Irene

Irene —

Thanks for the write-up. Confirming Greenline is asking to invoice quarterly with Net-90 for the first 12 months to align with our board funding cadence. We are cash-constrained through Q1 and cannot prepay the full 25%, sadly.

We could, however, do one of the following instead of full prepay:
- Provide a corporate guarantee from our parent company (I can send the legal contact)
- Agree to a partial 10% deposit at signature and the remaining billed quarterly

Our AP team (accounts-payable@greenlinehealth.com) will need the SOW and the final invoice schedule to issue the PO.

Irene —

I reviewed the SOW and credit form. High level:
- ACV: $320k first year (with expected expansion) — material but not deal-breaker.
- Credit: Greenline’s public filings show limited runway; CFO comment about parent guarantee is helpful but needs verification.
- Risk: granting Net-90 + quarterly invoices increases DSO exposure and collection overhead.

Recommend we escalate to Marissa for conditional approval. Suggested conditions:
1) Conditional approval tied to either a parent corporate guarantee OR a 20% deposit at signature (not 25%).
2) Add a 1.5%/month late fee effective after 60 days past invoice.
3) Require monthly usage reporting and a 30-day review cadence for the first 90 days.
4) Finance to place the deal on a 60-day credit hold if the first invoice is late.

I attached a short risk assessment (risk_assessment_greenline.xlsx) with modeled cashflow impact. If Marissa signs off, legal can produce a redline and we’ll capture the conditional terms in a one-page amendment.

-Jonas

Subject: Re: Proposal for payment-rhythm exemption (Greenline Health) — APPROVED (conditions)

Team —

After reviewing the recommendation I approve the billing-rhythm exception for Greenline Health with the following mandatory conditions:
1) Customer must provide either a verified parent corporate guarantee OR a 20% deposit at signature. We will accept Oliver’s 10% + an additional 10% via a scheduled ACH within 30 days if the guarantee is delayed, but the target is 20% at signing.
2) Include a 1.5%/month late fee clause after 60 days; Finance to enforce automatic hold on new work if an invoice is 45 days overdue.
3) Contract will include a three-month review clause (metrics: usage, outstanding AR) with an automatic reversion to monthly invoicing if delinquency occurs.
4) Any discount tied to these terms is capped at 8% (commercial discount cap).

Jonas/Legal: please prepare the amendment and route to Greenline via DocuSign. Finance: prepare the invoice schedule and label the deal ID DL-2026-1179 so collections can track.

Marissa
